title: Stellar Life Foundations

concepts.def: Collapsing cloud of gas heating up before fusion begins.
Stable phase fusing hydrogen into helium in the core.
Expanded cool low/medium mass star after main sequence.
Hot dense remnant of a low-mass star.
Explosive death of a massive star at end of life.
Tiny ultra-dense remnant left after a supernova.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gravity pulls a cloud of gas and dust (a nebula) inwards. As it collapses it heats up to form a protostar. When the core reaches ~10 million K, hydrogen fusion begins and a main sequence star is born.

Low/medium mass stars (like the Sun) swell to red giants, then shed a planetary nebula leaving a white dwarf. Massive stars become red supergiants, then explode as a supernova leaving a neutron star or black hole.
The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram plots luminosity (bottom to top) against temperature (right to left, hot on the left). Most stars sit on the diagonal main sequence band.
